raw_case_text:
A 42-year-old woman with stage 5D chronic kidney disease related to MYH9-related disease received her first kidney transplant from a familial living donor. Repeated anti-HLA antibody blood testing was negative, despite previous blood transfusions and pregnancies. The A, B, DR, and DQ HLA mismatches were 0/1/1/1, respectively. The CMV serostatus was D+/R-. Her immunosuppressive regimen consisted of an induction with antithymocyte globulins and a maintenance regimen with ciclosporin A, azathioprine, and steroids. She also received cotrimoxazole and vGCV prophylaxis for 6 months (900 mg/d). With the exception of two deep venous thrombosis episodes, the first seven months after transplantation was unremarkable with good transplant function (serum creatinine level = 100 mumol/L). One month after vGCV discontinuation on day (D) 222 after graft, she was admitted for a fever of 38.2 C and epigastric pain without diarrhea. Her biological tests revealed a severe lymphocytopenia (150/mm3). Her serum creatinine level was 122 mumol/L. The blood and urine cultures and liver and pancreatic tests were unremarkable, whereas her pp65 antigenemia was strongly positive (600 positive cells/200000 polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PC)). The chest X-ray and fundus examination did not suggest pulmonary or retinal CMV involvement. An upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed gastritis with a positive CMV polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Due to the diagnosis of possible CMV gastrointestinal disease, a first intravenous GCV treatment (10 mg/kg/d) was started together with a decrease in immunosuppression (half azathioprine dose), resulting in a slow but sustained decrease in the CMV antigenemia. Two months of GCV was needed to obtain viral clearance defined by two consecutive weekly negative antigenemia results.
One week after GCV discontinuation on D288, she was readmitted for fever recurrence and abdominal pain and a relapse of CMV disease was observed (antigenemia = 20 PC). No retinitis was found again. As digestive symptoms were similar to recent primary CMV infection, no new upper endoscopy was performed. A new GCV-based treatment (10 mg/kg/day) was started. No clinical or biological improvement was noted after two weeks of treatment (antigenemia = 115 PC) despite azathioprine withdrawal. Genotypic testing for ADR in the UL97 kinase gene revealed two common mutations (A594V and L595S) associated with moderate viral resistance for GCV and no mutation in the UL54 DNA polymerase gene. The kidney graft function was stable (serum creatinine level = 100 mumol/L). Thus, a second-line treatment with intravenous FOS (180 mg/kg/d) was initiated at D306. A fast decrease in the CMV viral load was observed that allowed FOS weaning at D320. A second relapse of CMV infection (same symptoms, antigenemia = 25 PC, blood quantitative CMV PCR = 351000 DNA copies/mL) at D329 led us to restart FOS at the same dose. Unfortunately, 6 days after this new FOS course a severe acute graft failure was noted (serum creatinine level = 450 mumol/L, blood ciclosporin trough level = 200 ng/mL) that was associated with an acute nephrotic syndrome (urinary protein creatinine ratio = 4.5 g/g and serum albumin = 2.6 g/dL). A transplant biopsy showed diffuse tubular necrosis and tubular and intraglomerular crystal deposits that obstructed capillaries and were suggestive of FOS nephropathy. No sign of acute rejection or CMV transplant infection was noted on the biopsy (Figure 1). At that time, the CMV antigenemia had become negative, blood CMV PCR was weak (1381 copies/mL), and FOS was stopped, which allowed a partial reversal of the glomerulopathy and transplant failure (serum creatinine level = 150 mumol/L and proteinuria = 1 g/d).
However, at D341 a third CMV relapse occurred (antigenemia = 78 PC, PCR = 141000 copies/mL). Because the FOS toxicity was recent, we decided to begin a double-dose of GCV therapy together with intravenous immunoglobulins (2 infusions of 0.3 g/kg/d at a 10-day interval) and a decrease in the ciclosporin target trough level (100 ng/mL). One month later, persistent low-grade symptoms and mild but positive CMV antigenemia (5-15 PC) reflected the failure of this regimen. A second genotypic testing for ADR revealed the same L595S mutation in the UL97 gene without mutation in the UL54 gene. To avoid new FOS toxicity, oral BCV was introduced (100 mg orally twice a week) at D376 for 21 days with good results on clinical and viral parameters (negative antigenemia and blood PCR after 17 days). A mild isolated cytolysis (alanine and aspartate aminotransferase (ALT and AST) = 137 and 104 IU/L, respectively) and moderate epigastric pain were observed during therapy. Liver ultrasonography was normal. The liver enzymes returned to normal levels and the abdominal pain disappeared after BCV discontinuation. Nevertheless, at D412 a 4th relapse was observed (antigenemia = 16 PC, blood PCR = 95700 copies/mL) and was again treated with BCV for 15 days (200 mg/week). After 15 days of BCV, persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain indicated a new upper gastrointestinal endoscopy together with a colonoscopy. CMV PCR biopsies of stomach and large bowel were positive (3380 and 3020 copies/mL, respectively). Blood CMV antigenemia and PCR were 9 PC and 38200 copies/mL, respectively, after 15 days of BCV. A new mild and isolated cytolysis (ALT = 143, ASAT = 155 IU/L) appearing at the same time led us to definitely stop BCV. Liver enzymes returned to normal levels after BCV discontinuation. No liver biopsy was performed. A third genotypic ADR test, performed at the end of the second course of BCV, revealed a novel F412L mutation in the UL54 DNA polymerase gene that was associated with moderate resistance for GCV and CDV but not FOS. Before reinitiating FOS, a new transplant biopsy was performed at D441 (serum creatinine = 150 mumol/L and proteinuria = 1 g/g). Seven of the 25 glomeruli were sclerotic. Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy were mild without crystals, rejection, or CMV signs. A new two-month course of intravenous FOS (50 mg/kg/d, dose tailored to decreased glomerular filtration rate) was necessary to achieve a complete resolution of CMV infection (negative antigenemia and PCR) without any new FOS nephropathy.  Figure 2 describes the course of the CMV disease together with the course of immunosuppression and blood lymphocyte counts.
Currently, the patient's overall condition is normal 6 months after the final treatment, without secondary CMV prophylaxis. Repeated CMV antigenemia tests have been negative, and the graft function remains stable (mean creatinine = 130 mumol/L, proteinuria = 0.6 g/g, without anti-HLA antibodies).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 42-year-old female living-donor kidney transplant recipient (CMV D+/R-) presented on post-transplant day 222 (1 month after stopping valganciclovir prophylaxis) with fever (38.2 °C) and epigastric pain, followed by four relapses of multidrug-resistant CMV gastrointestinal disease.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: After undergoing living-related kidney transplantation for MYH9-related stage 5D CKD (CMV D+/R-; rabbit ATG induction, cyclosporine A, azathioprine, and steroids maintenance, plus 6 months of valganciclovir 900 mg/day and cotrimoxazole prophylaxis; baseline creatinine 100 umol/L), the patient presented on day 222 (1 month post-valganciclovir cessation) with fever (38.2 °C) and epigastric pain without diarrhea, and subsequently experienced four consecutive relapses of fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea on days 288, 329, 341, and 412.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage 5D chronic kidney disease secondary to MYH9-related disease status post first living-related donor kidney transplantation (HLA A/B/DR/DQ mismatches 0/1/1/1; CMV serostatus D+/R-); two post-transplant deep venous thrombosis episodes; prior blood transfusions and pregnancies (anti-HLA antibody negative).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever (38.2 °C) and epigastric pain on day 222 (without diarrhea), followed across relapses by recurrent fever, abdominal pain, and persistent diarrhea (day 412), and transient drug-induced epigastric pain during brincidofovir therapy. Medications at day 222: cyclosporine A, azathioprine, and corticosteroids.

objective.physical_examination: Fever of 38.2 °C and epigastric tenderness on day 222; serial fundoscopic examinations showed no CMV retinitis.
objective.routine_investigations: Day 222 admission labs: severe lymphocytopenia (150/mm3), serum creatinine 122 umol/L (baseline 100 umol/L), normal blood/urine cultures and liver/pancreatic enzymes, normal chest X-ray, and strongly positive peripheral blood CMV pp65 antigenemia (600 positive cells / 200,000 PMNs). Subsequent CMV pp65 antigenemia and quantitative blood PCR across relapses: day 288 relapse 1 (antigenemia 20 rising to 115 PC); day 329 relapse 2 (antigenemia 25 PC, blood CMV PCR 351,000 copies/mL) complicated 6 days after restarting foscarnet by acute crystal nephropathy and nephrotic syndrome (creatinine 450 umol/L, cyclosporine trough 200 ng/mL, urine protein/creatinine ratio 4.5 g/g, serum albumin 2.6 g/dL; partially reversing to creatinine 150 umol/L and proteinuria 1 g/day after stopping foscarnet); day 341 relapse 3 (antigenemia 78 PC, blood PCR 141,000 copies/mL); day 376 brincidofovir course 1 (mild hepatic cytolysis ALT 137 IU/L, AST 104 IU/L, normal liver US); day 412 relapse 4 (antigenemia 16 PC, blood PCR 95,700 copies/mL; after 15d brincidofovir: antigenemia 9 PC, blood PCR 38,200 copies/mL, ALT 143 IU/L, AST 155 IU/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Day 222 upper GI endoscopy showed gastritis with positive gastric biopsy CMV PCR. Day 288 UL97/UL54 genotypic resistance testing revealed two UL97 mutations (A594V and L595S) conferring ganciclovir resistance (no UL54 mutation; L595S re-confirmed after relapse 3). Day 335 renal allograft biopsy during acute graft failure demonstrated diffuse acute tubular necrosis and obstructive intratubular and intraglomerular foscarnet crystal deposits without rejection or CMV inclusions. Day 427 upper GI endoscopy and colonoscopy biopsies were positive for CMV PCR in both the stomach (3,380 copies/mL) and colon (3,020 copies/mL), and genotypic resistance testing after the second brincidofovir course identified a novel UL54 DNA polymerase mutation (F412L) conferring cross-resistance to ganciclovir and cidofovir/brincidofovir while sparing foscarnet. Day 441 repeat renal allograft biopsy showed 7/25 sclerotic glomeruli and mild interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy with complete clearance of foscarnet crystals.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of late-onset primary D+/R- cytomegalovirus (CMV) gastritis and colitis complicated by sequential emergence of UL97 (A594V, L595S) and novel UL54 (F412L) antiviral resistance mutations and reversible foscarnet crystal nephropathy in a kidney transplant recipient. Managed initially with 2 months of IV ganciclovir (10 mg/kg/day) and azathioprine reduction/withdrawal, followed upon UL97-mediated ganciclovir failure by high-dose IV foscarnet (180 mg/kg/day, complicated during a second course by biopsy-proven glomerular/tubular crystal nephropathy), double-dose IV ganciclovir plus IVIG and cyclosporine trough reduction (to 100 ng/mL), and two courses of oral brincidofovir (BCV 100 mg twice weekly for 21 days at day 376, then 200 mg/week for 15 days at day 412, stopped due to reversible transaminitis and emergence of the UL54 F412L mutation). Ultimate sustained viral clearance and clinical cure were achieved with a 2-month course of GFR-adjusted low-dose intravenous foscarnet (50 mg/kg/day starting day 441), with negative CMV antigenemia and stable allograft function (creatinine 130 umol/L, proteinuria 0.6 g/g) at 6-month follow-up.
